nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / sandbox & compliance review
Legacy Oracle migration tooling & one-off data cleansing services
Cloud infra for staging/CI environment (first 3 months)

assumptions: No historical actuals/real spend data exist for this project yet; estimate is based purely on backlog scope and rate card, so confidence intervals are wider than they would be with delivery history.

1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended engineering effort for estimated items; unestimated items were sized by analogy to similarly-scoped estimated items (e.g. PW-8 legacy migration sized like a large 13-20pt effort, PW-2 design system sized like an 8-13pt effort).

Team capacity: 1.5 FTE Backend (~240 hrs/mo combined), 1.0 FTE Frontend (~160 hrs/mo), 0.6 FTE QA (~96 hrs/mo), 0.4 FTE DevOps (~64 hrs/mo). Allocated hours below are sized to be deliverable within roughly a 5-6 month timeline at this staffing level; QA and DevOps are thinly staffed relative to the 24-item backlog and will likely be the schedule bottleneck, especially DevOps at 0.4 FTE given CI/staging, observability, rate limiting and decommissioning work all compete for that single fractional resource.
PW-7 (Payment provider integration) and PW-8 (legacy data migration) are treated as the highest-risk/highest-effort items and are the main drivers of the High/Conservative scenario spread.
Low-priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) are included in the baseline estimate but are the first candidates for descoping if budget needs to be trimmed.
Non-labour costs are rough vendor/tooling estimates (Stripe compliance review, Oracle migration tooling, third-party accessibility audit, staging cloud infra) and are not backed by vendor quotes yet.

Scenario spread (Low/Most likely/High) reflects overall estimation uncertainty given no actuals exist, with Low assuming smoother integration work and High reflecting realistic risk on Stripe integration, data migration, and multi-currency complexity.

RBAC (PW-4), GDPR export (PW-9), and audit log (PW-10) are assumed to share a good amount of backend plumbing, so their combined hours are somewhat less than the sum of estimating them fully independently.
input.reasoning: Hours were allocated per backlog item using story points where given (assuming ~6-7 hours/point blended across roles) and analogy-based sizing for unestimated items, then aggregated per role and cross-checked against each role's FTE capacity to keep allocations proportionate (e.g., DevOps at 0.4 FTE only carries CI/staging, observability, rate limiting, and decommission work — capped around 180 hours total). Backend carries the largest share due to core domain logic (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, audit, multi-currency). Frontend carries dashboard, invoice UI, accessibility, responsive layout and admin back-office work. QA hours were sized at roughly 30% of dev effort, reflecting the 0.6 FTE constraint. Non-labour costs cover known third-party/tooling needs (Stripe compliance, Oracle migration tooling, accessibility audit, staging infra). Three scenarios (P20/P50/P80) were built around the summed baseline to reflect uncertainty, given no historical actuals exist to calibrate against. Priority breakdown was derived by mapping each backlog item's allocated labour cost to its stated priority band.

reductions.description: Descope Low-priority items PW-12 (support ticket submission), PW-18 (admin back-office), PW-19 (usage analytics), PW-23 (contract tests) and PW-24 (legacy decommission) from this phase and revisit in a later release.
reductions.effect: Removes ~17,000 USD of Low-priority backend/frontend/QA effort from the baseline; helpdesk sync and legacy shutdown can follow after go-live without blocking core launch.

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer allocation by focusing manual QA on Urgent/High priority flows only and relying on automated regression for Medium/Low items, cutting QA hours by ~25%.
reductions.effect: Cuts QA hours from 380 to ~285; acceptable given 0.6 FTE capacity constraint, but increases regression risk on Medium-priority features like search and multi-currency.

reductions.description: Defer multi-currency support (PW-14) to a post-launch phase, launching with USD only initially.
reductions.effect: Removes an estimated ~100 backend + 20 frontend hours tied to FX handling and settlement logic; can be reintroduced once core portal is live and stable.

reductions.description: Use a lighter-weight/managed accessibility audit (self-service automated scan plus spot-check) instead of a full third-party WCAG 2.2 AA audit.
reductions.effect: Reduces the non-labour accessibility audit line from 3,000 to about 1,000 USD; residual risk of missing some manual-only accessibility issues that automated tools can't catch.

reductions.description: Phase the legacy data migration (PW-8): migrate active/recent customer records first and defer full historical invoice-line migration by one quarter.
reductions.effect: Reduces upfront backend hours and migration tooling spend by deferring the bulk of the 2M invoice-line migration; requires a temporary read-only fallback to the legacy system for historical records.
